sources.label: TFB: Towards Comprehensive and Fair Benchmarking (arXiv 2403.20150)

findings.statement: Dropping the last incomplete batch during testing leads to unfair comparisons unless all methods use identical batch sizes.
findings.quote: Unless all methods use the same batch size, discarding the last batch of test samples is unfair, as the actual usage length of the test set is inconsistent.
findings.label: Protocol note

findings.statement: The authors acknowledge a long‑standing bug in the code framework that affected results, implying prior reported numbers may not be reproducible.
findings.quote: 🚩 News (2024.07): We have now fixed a long-standing bug (see description in FITS and TFB ) in the code framework and supplemented the full results (including MSE and MAE) of SparseTSF after fixing the bug in this table.
findings.label: Reproduction report

findings.statement: The paper’s evaluation may be flawed because a bug caused the last batch of test data to be dropped, potentially affecting reported performance.
findings.quote: We recently fixed a longstanding bug in this code framework (see description in TFB), which caused the last batch of data to be dropped during the testing phase.
findings.label: Protocol note

findings.statement: Reproduction attempts show significant discrepancies for sequence lengths 336 and 720, questioning the reproducibility of the reported results.
findings.quote: when I used the command sh scripts/SparseTSF/etth1.sh to reproduce the results from the paper, I found that the predictions with sequence lengths of 336 and 720 differ significantly from the results reported in the paper.
findings.label: Reproduction report

findings.statement: The evaluation bug affected the test results on ETTh1 and ETTh2, raising doubts about the reported numbers.
findings.quote: After the paper was accepted, we noticed the evaluation bug you mentioned, which primarily affected the test results on the ETTh1 and ETTh2 datasets.
findings.label: Note

findings.statement: Showing buggy results instead of the actual metrics is disingenuous and harms reproducibility.
findings.quote: I find this borderline disingenuous, you should have presented the actual metrics instead of the buggy one, regardless of your messaging.
findings.label: Reproduction report

summary.text: The paper suggests a very simple method that looks at patterns repeating over time to predict future values using only about one thousand adjustable settings. The data consists of hourly electricity‑usage readings from a transformer, collected over many days. A reported average forecast error of 0.359 means its predictions are, on average, quite close to the actual numbers.
